event_overview.title: About North Korea Missile Tests
event_overview.subject: North Korea Missile Tests
event_overview.summary: North Korea missile tests are launches conducted by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) as part of its ballistic-missile program, often drawing regional monitoring and international diplomatic responses. Coverage of launches around U.S.–Republic of Korea (ROK) exercises concerns the security environment on the Korean Peninsula; the exercises and the launches are distinct activities.

facts.label: International legal framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 1695, adopted on July 15, 2006, demanded that the DPRK suspend activities related to its ballistic-missile program and called on UN member states to prevent transfers supporting DPRK missile or weapons-of-mass-destruction programs.

facts.label: UN sanctions regime
facts.value: Security Council Resolution 1718, adopted on October 14, 2006, established sanctions measures that include prohibitions intended to prevent the DPRK from conducting ballistic-missile launches, as well as an arms embargo, asset freezes and travel restrictions for designated persons.

facts.label: Oversight body
facts.value: The UN Security Council’s 1718 Committee oversees sanctions relating to the DPRK; its mandate includes measures addressing materials, technology and support that could contribute to the DPRK’s nuclear or ballistic-missile programs.

facts.label: Geographic context
facts.value: The missile-launch and exercise reporting is centered on the Korean Peninsula and its surrounding region, where the ROK–U.S. alliance conducts combined readiness exercises and the DPRK’s missile activity is monitored as a regional-security issue.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the specified missile-launch developments in August and September 2026, not every DPRK weapons test, military exercise, sanctions action or diplomatic development.
